item: A volume backup copies the corpus instead of carrying a residual WAL, and counts the log in its space check
key_paths: src/backup/stream_backup.py; src/database/connect.py; src/backup/artifact.py; src/backup/merge.py; src/static/app-backup.js; tests/test_backup_snapshot.py; tests/test_write_gate_riders.py
summary: A free PASSIVE probe reads the checkpoint's own row: a reader that started after the last commit costs nothing, a reader older than a later commit makes the export copy the corpus through one read transaction into its staging dir on the destination drive (collection paused, no write gate), before the sizing, so the sizing, the free-space check and the facts see the copy. The check counts the store through the log (page_count x page_size) and refuses before a byte is copied in the standard words; a reader after the sizing is copied late in the same pause. Stop: an encrypted copy is interrupted within seconds, a plaintext copy ends first. Crash leftovers are swept by owner (pid + start time) and remembered destinations at boot on their own thread. Summary adds snapshot_s and snapshot_bytes; gate_held_s is the deciding window only; progress label x12 locales. No corpus-wal member is written; restore still reads one. Lesson: LESSONS.md, A BACKUP THAT CANNOT FOLD THE LOG INTO THE MAIN FILE COPIES THE CORPUS.
